title: How to Migrate a Website Without Losing Rankings

cover.alt: Conceptual miniature library volumes moving across a bridge along individually mapped routes

figures.title: A migration has three distinct stages
figures.summary: Preserve an evidence trail before changing the site.

items.label: Before launch
items.detail: Inventory URLs, save baseline data and map old pages to their destinations.

items.label: During launch
items.detail: Test redirects, preserve core content and update internal links.

items.label: After launch
items.detail: Submit the sitemap, crawl again and investigate indexing or routing errors.

figures.caption: The article's preparation, launch and monitoring sequence; no recovery timeline is guaranteed.

figures.title: Match the route to what happened to the content
figures.summary: Record the destination of every old page.

items.label: Unchanged URL
items.detail: Keep the route when the page remains there.

items.label: Moved page
items.detail: Point the old URL to its relevant new equivalent.

items.label: Consolidated content
items.detail: Choose the destination that covers the former page's subject.

items.label: Verification
items.detail: Check the response status and final location.

figures.caption: Decision cases from the redirect map and testing examples.
